chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Khashshab, from Ibn Baqqah, from Amr ibn Jumi'ah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever finds a piece of bread and eats it, it will be a good deed for him; and whoever finds it in dirt, washes it, then picks it up, it will be seventy good deeds for him.'

key_terms.كِسْرَة: A piece or fragment of bread/food

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for picking up and eating a piece of bread that fell on the ground?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on frugality and reverence for sustenance, linking physical cleanliness with spiritual reward. The distinction between merely consuming a found morsel and the multiplied reward for cleaning one soiled by dirt reflects the principle that removing impurity (najis) from food elevates the act of eating from necessity to worship. This practice is rooted in the Prophetic tradition of valuing every grain, reinforcing gratitude (shukr) for Allah's provisions.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Khashaab, from Ibn Baqqa, from Amro Bin Jumi’a who said,

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who finds one crumb, so he eats it, would have a Reward for him; and the one who finds it in dirt, so he washes it, then raises it, would have seventy Rewards for him’.
en.sarwar: 5. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Khashshab from ibn Baqqah from ‘Amr ibn Jami’ who has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith. ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “If one finds pieces of food and eats them it is one good deed, and if one finds them in unclean places, then washes them, then picks them up, he will have seventy good deeds recorded for him.’””
